advances: Sampled-endpoint topology on a fixed five-site positive support.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The baseline is realized by the two affine roofs $x=\pm(13/2-z)$ on $[0,4]$. Let $[l_i,h_i]$ be the sampled intervals and let $M$ be their total length. At a mark $(p,y)$, the upper cap of slope $v$ has mass $F_p(v)=\sum_i\min(w_i,\max(0,h_i-y-v(i-p)))$. The lower cap has mass $M-F_p(v)$. The accepted finite slope rule applies to these five bounded intervals: the only finite knots are $(e-y)/(i-p)$, $i\ne p$, for endpoints $e=l_i,h_i$. Each tail has the value at the extreme adjacent knot. The baseline knots and upper masses at $y=0$, in increasing order, are as follows.

| $p$ | Knots | Masses in the same order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $-13/2,-9/2,-7/4,-5/6,5/6,7/4,9/2,13/2$ | $53/2,57/2,57/2,80/3,55/3,33/2,33/2,37/2$ |
| $2$ | $-11/2,-7/2,-13/4,-5/4,5/4,13/4,7/2,11/2$ | $33/2,37/2,37/2,45/2,45/2,53/2,53/2,57/2$ |

For the perturbed marks use $y_1=(c_0+c_1+c_2)/3$ and $y_2=c_2$. Their changes are at most $1/100$. Each knot shifts by at most $2/100$, while adjacent knots in both baseline tables differ by at least $1/4$, so the complete order persists. The two minimum knots at base $1$ bound a plateau of upper caps cutting exactly fibers $0,1,2$ properly and missing $3,4$. Their mass, even at the bounding knots by continuity, is $\sum_{i=0}^2 h_i-3y_1=q_1$. The maximum knots bound the complementary plateau where the lower cap takes $3y_1-\sum_{i=0}^2 l_i=q_1$, so their upper mass is $M-q_1$. The status patterns persist because the knot order of the endpoints for every unanchored fiber persists, and the own mark remains interior. At base $2$ the two far plateaus retain half the own interval and respectively the two right or two left intervals, giving upper masses $q_2$ and $M-q_2$.

The nearest baseline nonextremal mass to either extreme in both tables is at distance at least $11/6$. For an endpoint perturbation of radius $1/100$, any one summand of a knot mass changes by at most $(4+2|i-p|)/100$, from changes of at most $2/100$ in width and $(2+2|i-p|)/100$ in the unclipped mass. This is less than $55/100$ summed over five sites. Each $q_p$ moves by at most $5/100$, and $M-q_p$ by at most $15/100$. Hence every noncritical knot stays strictly between the two comparison masses. The smallest vertical mass is $24$ at base $1$ and $21$ at base $2$ at baseline, and changes by at most $10/100$. These purely base caps also exceed $q_p$. The finite slope rule therefore gives the claimed exact depths at the two marks.

For the upper bound everywhere, use the two caps $x-2(z-1)\ge y_1$ and $-x-2(z-1)\ge-y_1$. They retain the indicated proper block $0,1,2$ and miss $3,4$, since their fixed slopes lie strictly inside the relevant baseline knot ranges and move relative to knots by at most $2/100$. Their masses both equal $q_1$ and their margins sum to $-4(z-1)$, covering every line at $z\le1$. The other pair is $x+10(z-2)\ge c_2$ and $-x+10(z-2)\ge-c_2$. They retain half of fiber $2$ and all of $3,4$, and miss $0,1$. Their margins sum to $20(z-2)$, covering every line at $z\ge2$, and both masses are $q_2$. This proves the global formula. At baseline, the exposed extreme maxima are $13/2$ and $5/2$. At base $3$ steep opposite height cuts isolate half the own interval and the smaller right tail, bounding depth by $7/2+5$. At base $1$ or $2$ the covering pair shares its mark. Any other point of the same fiber lies strictly inside one cap, which can be shifted toward the point by a small positive amount and lose positive length from the own fiber. Thus only the two stated points are deepest at baseline.

Concavity of the widths yields $w_0+w_4\le2w_2$ and $w_1+w_3\le2w_2$, hence $M\le5w_2$. With $Q=\max(q_1,q_2)$,
$$
3Q\ge2q_1+q_2=M+w_2/2\ge11M/10.
$$
Equality requires a tie and equality in both midpoint concavity inequalities. In particular equality for the extremes at their midpoint forces all intervening widths to lie on the same affine chord, by the monotonicity of consecutive slopes. Write $w_i=A+Bi$; the tie gives $A=-13B/2$. Since the difference of the upper concave and lower convex endpoint sequences is affine, both endpoint sequences are affine. The resulting affine centers and proportional widths are exactly the orbit under translation, shear and positive scaling, which preserve normalized depth.

Normalize each array continuously by scaling its total mass to $45$ and subtracting the affine height function interpolating its extreme centers. The normalized equality orbit is then a singleton. A nonincreasing path starting there cannot leave it while the sampled arrays remain positive: its preimage is closed by continuity, and is open relative to the positive path because the local lower bound and its equality characterization apply in the endpoint neighborhood. The interval before a first collapse is connected, so the normalized widths stay fixed there. A collapse with positive limiting total length is incompatible with those fixed normalized widths.

statement:
At bases $0,\ldots,4$ take centered intervals of widths $(13,11,9,7,5)$. They have total mixed length $45$, global raw depth $33/2$, and precisely the deepest points $(1,0),(2,0)$. For any compatible positive array at these sites whose endpoints each differ from the corresponding original endpoint by at most $1/100$, let $w_i,c_i$ be its widths and centers. Its global raw depth is exactly $\max(q_1,q_2)$, where
$$
q_1=(w_0+w_1+w_2)/2,\qquad q_2=w_2/2+w_3+w_4.
$$
The respective depths $q_1,q_2$ are attained at $(1,(c_0+c_1+c_2)/3)$ and $(2,c_2)$. The normalized maximum is at least $11/30$ there. Equality holds exactly for widths proportional to the original widths and affine centers. Modulo continuous height translation, shear and positive scaling, the baseline is a strict local minimum in sampled-endpoint topology. There is no continuous path of these five sampled endpoint pairs starting there, with nonincreasing normalized depth, that collapses a fiber while some positive length remains.
title: A strict fixed-support depth minimum with five interval fibers
